A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching algorithms and main guarantees. The main text, equations, figures and complete appendices support comparison. The principal proofs in v1 Appendices C–E correspond to v2 Appendices B–D.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical algorithms, learning bounds and proofs, including its appendices, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. Its new figures illustrate algorithms rather than empirical results.

M1.justification: The recursive splitting schemes, sampled ERM ensembles, 11/243 and 232/243 voting thresholds, tie-breaking ERM and final selection against the Hanneke et al. learner are retained. The overview moved from v1 Appendix B to v2 Section 3.2 describes the same procedure despite classifier renaming and notation corrections.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or concrete evaluation scenarios. Both study distribution-free binary PAC learning over arbitrary domains and hypothesis classes of finite VC dimension.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimentally evaluated baselines. ERM and Hanneke et al. (2024) retain their theoretical comparison and algorithm-combination roles; the added citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an experimental evaluation protocol. The sample partitions and sampling requirements describe the retained theoretical algorithms, rather than changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments or case studies. The new discussion of Chernoff arguments concerns mathematical reasoning, rather than supplementary empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Concentration inequalities and failure probabilities are components of theoretical proofs, whose revisions are assessed under T1.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added, removed or revised. The principal learning guarantees retain their rates and leading constants, including 2.1 in the main theorem and 2.0888 in v1 Theorem D.1/v2 Theorem C.1. Intermediate proof-bound corrections are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 1.1 corrects the lower-bound probability from 1−δ to δ. Section 3.2 changes the recursive-error multiplier from 112 to 3160, incorporating the branch-selection factor, and replaces an exact filtered-sample-size identity with a Θ relation. New Appendix A.1 adds reasoning using Sauer–Shelah and ERM lower bounds against a simple Chernoff approach. The main theorems and detailed proof framework remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.1 explicitly state optimality for τ=O(d/m), broadening the emphasized regime from v1's τ≈d/m. v2 also specifies the improvement regime over Hanneke et al. and the remaining polylogarithmic gap. These refine the stated contribution's scope without changing the main bound.

C2.justification: New Remark 3.1 distinguishes intuitive stabilization from established algorithmic stability, explaining the obstacle posed by overlapping training samples. Appendix A.1 newly discusses why straightforward Chernoff arguments are insufficient and emphasizes that the learner requires no knowledge of τ.

D1.justification: Both versions supply the same substantive pseudocode, voting thresholds, sampling requirements and ERM-oracle complexity information. The relocated overview clarifies existing specifications; no implementation, hardware, measured runtime or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bousquet and Elisseeff (2002), Bousquet et al. (2020), Høgsgaard (2025), and Maurer and Pontil (2009), supporting targeted discussion of stability, ERM limitations and related learning bounds. It also specifies the prior work's τ regime and narrows the positioning from considering τ dependence to optimal τ dependence.

P1.justification: The main exposition receives substantial rewriting and condensation, especially the proof sketch. The algorithm overview moves from Appendix B into Section 3.2, the contents page disappears, and Appendix A.1 is added. Structural defects also appear: Appendix A and A.1 are duplicated in v2, and several problem or lemma references are incorrectly called theorems.

P2.justification: v2 comprehensively changes typography, title formatting, text density and equation layout, placing the introduction on the opening page. New Figure 1 illustrates recursive splitting and Figure 2 diagrams the complete learner. Algorithm displays are repositioned, with an additional duplicate accompanying the repeated Appendix A.

improvement.justification: The corrected lower-bound probability and recursive-error constant improve technical accuracy, while the figures and relocated algorithm overview make the construction easier to follow. Scope and stability qualifications also help. These provide a modest net benefit, limited by the duplicated Appendix A/A.1 and incorrect theorem references; the central guarantees remain unchanged.
